title: Breakthrough Advertising (Eugene Schwartz, 1966; current hardcover reprint)
publisher: Titans Marketing (Brian Kurtz), the book's rights holder
supports: The book and its 1966 text; dominant desire, channelling existing desire, and segmenting by awareness and market sophistication, summarised in the canon

title: Books (How Brands Grow, How Brands Grow Part 2, Building Distinctive Brand Assets)
supports: Byron Sharp, How Brands Grow (Oxford University Press, 2010); Romaniuk and Sharp, How Brands Grow Part 2 revised (OUP, 2021); Jenni Romaniuk, Building Distinctive Brand Assets (OUP, 2018), covering taglines, jingles and characters as brand cues

title: The next chapter for The Long and The Short of It (13 September 2023)
supports: Binet and Field's 2013 finding of a roughly 60:40 brand-to-activation split, about 62:38 in the 2018 follow-up, and the warning about over-reliance on short-term metrics

title: A Slice of Lemon: a summary of Lemon by Orlando Wood
supports: Lemon published by the IPA in October 2019; analysis of 620 Coronation Street break ads from 2004 to 2018; left-brain and right-brain ad features; argument that flat, left-brained ads are less effective, based on System1 data

title: YouTube ABCDs: video ad best practices (Ariane Le Port, April 2022)
supports: Attention, Branding, Connection, Direction; YouTube described as almost entirely sound-on; average 30% lift in short-term sales likelihood and 17% in long-term brand contribution (Google/Kantar Link AI, 2021)

title: When it comes to advertising effectiveness, what is key? (October 2017)
supports: Project Apollo (2006): 65% of a brand's sales lift from advertising came from creative; NCSolutions analysis of nearly 500 FMCG campaigns (2016 to Q1 2017): media's share of the effect rose to 36% from 15% over 11 years

title: How Not To Run an A/B Test (18 April 2010, updated 2013)
supports: Peeking inflates false positives (26.1% in the worked example where 5% was intended); fix the sample size in advance; rule of thumb n = 16 sigma squared over delta squared

title: Split testing (Marketing API guide)
supports: Split tests and the Creative Test type (2 to 7 creative variants, one ad per cell); no audience overlap between cells; test one variable; set the confidence level before the test; example windows of 7 and 14 days

title: Meta Andromeda: supercharging Advantage+ automation with the next-gen personalized ads retrieval engine (2 December 2024)
supports: Retrieval narrows tens of millions of ad candidates to a few thousand; Meta expects creative volume to grow with generative AI; Meta's own figures of +6% recall and +8% ads quality on selected segments

title: AI innovation in Meta's ads ranking driving advertiser performance (27 March 2025)
supports: As advertisers upload more creatives for a diversification strategy, Andromeda picks the right creative for each person; 8% increase in ads quality; GEM's Reels launch raised conversions by up to 5% (Meta's figures)

title: Creative fatigue recommendations in Meta Ads Manager
supports: Meta's Help Center does not render for automated fetches; confirmed by a WebSearch result showing this exact page. Creative fatigue is when an audience has seen the same creative too many times, and Ads Manager gives recommendations for it

title: Instagram Reels ad specs (Meta Ads Guide)
supports: 9:16 at 1440 x 2560; keep 14% of the top, 35% of the bottom and 6% of each side free of text, logos and key elements; captions recommended; sound strongly recommended; original or royalty-free audio

title: Facebook Feed video ad specs (Meta Ads Guide)
supports: 4:5 at 1440 x 1800; primary text 50 to 150 characters and headline 27 characters; captions and sound optional but recommended

title: Meta Advertising Standards
supports: Policy structure (prohibited practices, restricted goods, objectionable content, IP, political ads, EU DSA transparency); review typically within 24 hours; appeals through Account Quality

title: Health and wellness (Advertising Standards; version of 23 July 2026)
supports: Weight-loss and cosmetic procedure ads targeted 18+; no side-by-side weight-loss transformations; no close-ups pinching fat; no negative self-perception; rules on before-and-after for cosmetic procedures

title: Privacy violations and personal attributes (Advertising Standards)
supports: Ads must not assert or imply personal attributes (health, finances, religion, sexual orientation and others), with acceptable and unacceptable copy examples

title: Ad Library tools (updated 24 August 2023)
supports: The Ad Library holds all active ads; social issue, election and political ads kept 7 years; EU-delivered ads archived for one year after last impression; paid partnership branded content; Ad Library API

title: About video ad formats
supports: Skippable in-stream can be skipped after 5 seconds; bumpers up to 6 seconds; non-skippable 15 to 60 seconds by subtype; Shorts ads under 60 seconds recommended; Views renamed TrueView views as of October 2025

title: About YouTube ads and view metrics
supports: A TrueView view counts at 30 seconds or the end (or a click); bumpers and non-skippable ads do not count views; view rate is views over impressions, about 10 to 15% called average for in-stream; quartile metrics are directional

title: Google Ads policies (overview)
supports: Four policy areas: prohibited content, prohibited practices, restricted content and features, editorial and technical; examples of generic and gimmicky ad text

title: Misrepresentation
supports: Sub-policies including unreliable claims, clickbait that uses negative life events, misleading ad design, manipulated media, dishonest pricing and unavailable offers

title: TikTok Auction In-Feed Ads (specifications)
supports: TikTok blocks automated fetches; confirmed by WebSearch results showing this exact page. Vertical 9:16 recommended at 540 x 960 or more; 16:9 and 1:1 accepted; up to 4 caption lines shown; safe zone depends on dimension, caption length and add-ons, with downloadable safe-zone files

title: Video Advertising Guide for Small Businesses
supports: TikTok blocks automated fetches; confirmed by a WebSearch result showing this exact page. TikTok recommends videos up to 60 seconds and says 21 to 34 seconds performs best (TikTok's own claim)

title: Pinterest product specs
supports: 2:3 (1000 x 1500) recommended; titles up to 100 characters with the first 40 shown in feeds; descriptions hidden in feeds; video 4 seconds to 15 minutes, 6 to 15 seconds recommended

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Endorsements must reflect honest experience; disclosures go in the video itself, near the endorsement, audible and visible; description-only or end-of-video disclosures unlikely to work; results claims read as typical

title: FTC announces final rule banning fake reviews and testimonials (14 August 2024)
supports: Bans fake testimonials including AI-generated ones attributed to people who do not exist or had no experience, undisclosed insider endorsements and fake social indicators; civil penalties for knowing violations

title: Beauty and cosmetics: the use of production techniques (18 August 2025)
supports: Filters and retouching must not exaggerate what a product can do; disclaimers do not cure a misleading image; before-and-after images must be representative; keep records of techniques used

title: The (mis)use of social media beauty filters when advertising cosmetic products (11 February 2021)
supports: Rulings against Skinny Tan and We Are Luxe (Tanologist) Instagram Stories in which filters darkened influencers' skin, exaggerating the tanning products' effect; the advertiser is responsible

title: The Digital Services Act (last update 1 October 2026)
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Ads must be labelled and show who placed them and why they are shown; very large platforms keep public ad repositories; no ads based on sensitive data; no targeted ads to children; dark patterns banned

title: AI Act (regulatory framework for AI)
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: AI Act transparency rules come into effect in August 2026; deepfakes and certain AI-generated content must be clearly labelled; voluntary Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI content; guidelines dated 20 July 2026
